title: Cabinet Approves Rs 84,084 Crore 'Samudra Manthan' Scheme for Oil and Gas Exploration
excerpt: India's cabinet greenlit a massive exploration push to reduce crude oil import dependence, with incentives spanning deep-water drilling and unconventional hydrocarbon development.
body:
• The Union Cabinet approved the Rs 84,084 crore Samudra Manthan scheme to boost domestic oil and gas exploration.
  • The program targets deep-water, ultra-deep-water, and unconventional hydrocarbon resources across India's sedimentary basins.
  • India imports over 85% of its crude oil, making energy security a persistent strategic vulnerability.
  • The scheme offers production-linked incentives and marketing freedom to attract private and foreign investment.

India's Union Cabinet approved the Rs 84,084 crore Samudra Manthan scheme on Thursday, launching the country's most ambitious push to expand domestic oil and gas production in decades.

Scope and Structure

Named after the mythological churning of the ocean, Samudra Manthan targets exploration and production across India's under-explored sedimentary basins. The scheme covers deep-water and ultra-deep-water drilling, shale gas development, coal-bed methane extraction, and gas hydrate exploration — areas where India has significant geological potential but limited commercial activity.

The government will offer production-linked incentives, revenue-sharing flexibility, and marketing freedom for extracted gas to attract private operators and international oil companies. The scheme also includes provisions for technology transfer and partnerships with established deep-water operators.

"The Union Cabinet approved the Rs 84,084 crore Samudra Manthan scheme to boost domestic oil and gas exploration."

Why It Matters

India currently imports over 85% of its crude oil requirements, spending more than $120 billion annually on petroleum imports. This dependency has left the economy vulnerable to global price shocks — most recently visible during the Iran-related supply disruptions that pushed fuel costs higher.

Domestic production has stagnated around 29-30 million metric tonnes annually for over a decade, even as consumption has risen steadily with economic growth and an expanding vehicle fleet. The gap between production and consumption widened further in FY26.

Exploration Targets

The government estimates India's 26 sedimentary basins hold substantial untapped reserves. Only seven basins have seen commercial production, and large swathes of the Krishna-Godavari, Andaman, and Mahanadi basins remain either unexplored or underexplored.

Samudra Manthan aims to bring at least 10 additional blocks into active exploration within the first three years, with commercial production targets set for 2032-2035.

Investment Implications

The scheme is expected to catalyze private sector participation through competitive bidding rounds under the Open Acreage Licensing Policy. ONGC and Oil India, the state-owned exploration giants, are likely to anchor the initial exploration phase, with international partners expected for technically complex deep-water projects.

For NRI investors, the scheme signals a long-term structural shift in India's energy policy — from import dependence to domestic production incentives, with implications for oil marketing companies, drilling services providers, and upstream E&P stocks listed on Indian exchanges.
nri_angle: Major policy shift for India's energy security, with investment implications for NRIs holding upstream and E&P stocks.
